meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Grand Duchy of Luxembourg (no sub-state tax distinction for SCSp registration)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (based on French Civil Code and Luxembourg Commercial Code; strong EU directive overlay)

Double Taxation Treaties with more than 75 jurisdictions, including Germany, France, Belgium, Netherlands, United States, United Kingdom, Japan, Switzerland

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant le Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), as amended by Loi du 25 mars 2020; Directive (EU) 2015/849 (4AMLD) and Directive (EU) 2018/843 (5AMLD) as transposed in Luxembourg law; Regulation (EU) 2018/1672 on cash controls.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each natural-person UBO and the SCSp general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national identity authority of the UBO's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing country; if issued by a non-Hague state, consular legalization at the Luxembourg embassy or consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or current extract from the company register of any legal-person shareholder or general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original country's company registry or trade register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille from the register's state authority; for non-Hague countries, consular legalization via Luxembourg diplomatic mission

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial ownership chain attestation and UBO disclosure declaration from each intermediary legal entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Legal representative or registered agent of each foreign entity in the ownership chain
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature followed by Hague Apostille in the country of execution; non-Hague states require consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, legal representatives, and commercial agents against the UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, Luxembourg national freezing list maintained by the Ministry of Finance, and OFAC SDN List where USD payment rails are used. PEP status must be assessed using international standards (FATF, EU PEP directive) and verified through up-to-date PEPS databases at formation, on any ownership change, and on any trigger event. Ongoing transaction monitoring and enhanced due diligence apply under the Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004, as amended, and CSSF guidance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés / RBE online portal via MyGuichet
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be registered in Latin script only. French, German, or Luxembourgish names are accepted without transliteration. Names in other languages must be accompanied by an approved Latin-script transliteration; the transliteration must be identical to the name used in the SCSp partnership deed and in all subsequent RCS filings. Non-Latin scripts are not accepted in official corporate filings.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Bank, banque, assurance, réassurance, trust, fiduciaire (requires prior CSSF authorization)
SICAV, SICAF, FCP, OPC, fonds, asset-management terms (requires financial-sector license)
Luxembourg, Grand-Duché, or Luxembourgish state derivatives (requires prior Ministry of Justice authorization to avoid false sovereign association)
Words contrary to public order, good morals, or contrary to mandatory Luxembourg public policy
Misleading terms implying a different legal form, unlimited liability, or greater capital than actually exists
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: An RCS name reservation may be renewed for successive 30-day periods while incorporation documents are pending. If the name is rejected, the applicant must file a written administrative request for reconsideration with the director of the Luxembourg Business Registers within 15 calendar days of the refusal notification. If the refusal is upheld, the applicant may file a substantive appeal with the Administrative Tribunal (Tribunal administratif) within three months of the confirmation, in accordance with the Luxembourg law of 19 December 2002 on the register of commerce and companies and the general administrative procedure act.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible as the sole statutory registered office for an SCSp. The registered office must be a material, physically accessible address in Luxembourg where statutory records, tax files, and the central administration can be examined and where legal process may be served. A serviced office from a licensed corporate service provider is acceptable if it includes a physical reception address, mail handling, and secure document storage. A pure PO Box or fully virtual address without physical presence is rejected.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate for a low-risk digital webtoon publishing entity. Estimated unannounced on-site inspection probability is 5-8% per active year. The likelihood rises to 10-20% if the UBO chain includes multi-layer offshore nominee companies or if local substance indicators (central administration, decision-making in Luxembourg) are questioned by tax or RCS authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 101-1 to 101-11 (Société en Commandite Spéciale), together with Articles 18 to 22 on partnerships and Article 1 on the general corporate regime.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS), operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), 1-3 Boulevard de la Foire, L-1528 Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Constitution Deed and Articles of Association (Acte de constitution et statuts) - executed by private deed or before a Luxembourg notary, filed with the RCS, and published in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The SCSp has no legal minimum capital pursuant to Article 101-4 of the 1915 Law; the deed freely fixes the amount and nature of contributions. Cash contributions do not legally require a blocked escrow account, though a Luxembourg bank confirmation of contribution receipt (attestation de blocage) is customary for third-party and financing purposes.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: First Resolutions of the Founding General Partner of [NAME] SCSp. The form of a Société en Commandite Spéciale under Articles 101-1 et seq. of the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 is adopted; the draft articles of association are approved verbatim. The initial contribution of the limited partner, in the amount set out in the subscription schedule, is accepted; no statutory escrow applies. The registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg; the domiciliation agent is instructed to file the corresponding declaration with the RCS. [Name] is appointed general partner and [Name] manager, acting singly, with authority to open bank accounts, execute contracts, file tax returns, and complete all statutory registrations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the constitution deed and articles of association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founding partners (associés) or a Luxembourg notary; notarial form is required if contributions comprise real property. The deed may be drafted in French, German or English, with a French translation for RCS filing.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the statuts specifying corporate name, registered office, corporate purpose, duration, identity of the general partner and the limited partner(s), amount of each contribution, profit-sharing rules, and the management clause (gérance). Sign the deed; private deeds may be signed electronically. If the general partner is a corporate entity, a certified resolution of that entity must evidence the representative's authority.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of association (statuts) for the SCSp
Identity documents (passport) of all partners and managers
Registration extract and articles of the corporate general partner, if any
Corporate resolution of the general partner authorizing the constitution
LBR name reservation confirmation (negative certificate of name availability)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry challenges the name or clause wording, re-reserve the name with LBR and execute a supplementary deed; if the notary refuses due to incomplete anti-money-laundering identification, supply ID, source-of-funds evidence, and notarially certified powers.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS deposit, registration, and legal publication in the RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) - Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), via physical counters or the eRCS online portal (lbr.lu).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed constitution deed together with the statement of subscription and conformity (déclaration de souscription et de conformité) within 10 days of signature. Pay the filing fee. The RCS assigns the registration number (numéro d'immatriculation) and, after verification, orders publication of a summary of the deed in the RESA.
required_dossiers: Signed constitution deed (original, two copies)
Statement of subscription and conformity under Article 101-5 of the 1915 Law
Proof of registered office: lease, ownership deed, or licensed fiduciary domiciliation agreement
Identity documents of the appointed representatives
Criminal record extract (bulletin n°3) for each natural-person manager or foreign equivalent
Certificate of non-bankruptcy for the corporate general partner
Bank confirmation of contribution payment, if contributions are paid up
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS queries the file for incomplete proofs or signature legalization, remedy within one month of the notice; if registration is refused, appeal to the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within two months of the refusal notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax and VAT registration (matricule, VAT number, and EU OSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for the business tax number; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and the EU One-Stop-Shop (OSS), filed through the guichet.lu single window.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form 1 with the ACD to obtain the 11-digit matricule d'imposition within 5 to 10 business days of RCS registration. Register with the AEDT under Article 4 of the Luxembourg VAT law for VAT on B2C digital services (standard rate 17%). If sales to final consumers in other EU member states exceed EUR 10,000 per calendar year, register for the OSS scheme in the AEDT portal and declare all cross-border B2C supplies on one return.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Constitution deed and RESA publication extract
Matrixicle confirmation from the RCS
Identity documents and appointment act of the manager
Proof of Luxembourg bank account (IBAN) for VAT refunds
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ACD or AEDT issues an information request, answer within the notified period; contest the VAT effective date or assessment by appeal to the Director of the AEDT within three months under Article 77 of the Luxembourg VAT Law.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social security and employer obligations registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS), 4 rue Mercier, L-2144 Luxembourg, via the guichet.lu employer portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the employer entity with the CCSS to obtain the employer affiliation number within eight days of the first hiring; the general partner assumes employer obligations as the SCSp lacks legal personality for employment purposes. Enroll each employee and any remunerated manager for health, pension, accident, and dependency insurance. File monthly contributions through the CCSS online portal.
required_dossiers: CCSS employer registration form (formulaire d'affiliation)
Matricule d'imposition and RCS extract
Employment contracts or management agreement of the gérant
Identity documents and residence certificates of employees
Bank account details for CCSS debits
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS disputes the employer number, contribution basis, or affiliation date, submit a rectification request via the online portal within one month; appeal to the Conseil arbitral de la sécurité sociale within 40 days of the notification.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for pure digital webtoon publishing. If the company later opens physical retail or warehouse premises, the Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie - Direction des PME) would require an establishment authorization (autorisation d'établissement) under the Law of 2 September 2011; for the present intangible B2C digital activity, no such authorization is mandated.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No sectoral operating permit required for ISIC 9000 digital publishing. Complementary registrations only: RCS registration, Luxembourg VAT registration, and EU OSS registration for cross-border B2C digital supplies.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Environmental Agency of Luxembourg), 1 avenue du Rock'n'Roll, L-4361 Esch-sur-Alzette, Luxembourg
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - no Class 1-4 classified installation under the Law of 7 October 2011; the activity is entirely intangible and produces no industrial emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial discharge, VOC, or wastewater thresholds apply. General obligations include: EU WEEE Directive 2012/19/EU and RoHS Directive 2011/65/EU for end-of-life hardware and e-waste disposal; EU Code of Conduct for Data Centres for server energy efficiency; waste handling in accordance with the Luxembourg Waste Management Law of 21 March 2017 through certified recyclers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For a standard Luxembourg office (up to 1,000 m2 and fewer than 50 employees): communal fire safety certificate and CGDIS inspection of the premises; occupational safety clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering workstation ergonomics, electrical safety, and building access. Where the registered office is provided by a licensed domiciliation agent, the agent's building safety compliance certificate and communal fire certificate at fit-out are sufficient evidence.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in conjunction with the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance (Direction de la Trésorerie) and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for payment, foreign-exchange intermediation and financial-market supervision.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area jurisdiction with full convertibility on both current and capital account transactions by virtue of Articles 63-65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There is no exchange-control licensing, prior-authorisation, quota or investment-screening requirement for ordinary commercial or treasury flows of an SCSp. Profit remittances to non-resident partners are legally unrestricted, and distributions of an SCSp are not subject to Luxembourg withholding tax when addressed to corporate or qualifying partnership partners, subject to substance, anti-abuse and beneficial-ownership conditions. Residual hurdles are limited to AML/KYC verification of beneficial owners, CRS/FATCA reporting, and the BCL's statistical balance-of-payments reporting on cross-border transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Not applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, conversion, retention or repatriation timeline on export proceeds. Webtoon subscription and licensing revenue received in USD, EUR, KRW or JPY may be freely kept in foreign currency, converted into euro, or used directly for outbound royalty settlements. The only mandatory obligations are the BCL's monthly/quarterly balance-of-payments statistical declarations triggered by cross-border payment activity above the de-minimis reporting threshold (generally EUR 12.5 million aggregate annual turnover per resident reporting entity) and standard tax/CRS disclosures; no mandatory conversion ratio exists.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Contribution Escrow Account and Operational Current Account
Operational Current and E-Commerce Settlement Account
Operational Treasury and FX Hedging Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Quintet Private Bank (formerly KBL European Private Bankers)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Private Banking Wealth and Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-Low for primary treasury use. EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions passportable into Luxembourg under PSD2 (e.g., Adyen, Stripe, Payoneer, CurrencyCloud) can legitimately execute SEPA, SEPA Instant and cross-border collections for Apple IAP and Google Play Billing settlement, as well as automated payouts to webtoon creators and translators. However, an EMI cannot provide a depositary, credit, capital-escrow or investment-custody relationship; its safeguarding obligations require client funds to be segregated in a shell account held with a Luxembourg/EEA credit institution or central bank, effectively making the domestic bank the ultimate custodian of the SCSp's cash pool. Offshore EMIs headquartered outside the EEA (UK FCA-authorised, US FinCEN MSB, Singapore MAS-licensed) do not enjoy EU passporting rights and require local CSSF/BCL authorisation or engagement via a white-label Luxembourg partner; therefore they must be confined to payment-processor functionality and never treated as treasury counterparties.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the SCSp, the general partner's authorised managers and all ultimate beneficial owners holding more than 25% are subject to a structured KYC interrogation. CSSF-blessed video-identification with liveness checks is accepted by some institutions for overseas-resident UBOs, but the majority of tier-1 Luxembourg banks require at minimum one physical meeting of the statutory manager (or the presentation of a notarised and apostilled power of attorney in favour of a Luxembourg-resident authorised signatory) before account activation. Passive non-resident limited partners may be onboarded fully remotely when their identity and source of wealth are evidenced by certified passport copies, tax residence certificates, and CRS/FATCA self-certification forms.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident limited partner owning ≥25% of the SCSp with a complex or opaque personal wealth structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fund-flow narrative; 12 months of underlying bank statements; tax residence certificates; notarised corporate registry extracts or trust deeds; source-of-wealth report; CV of the UBO; signed declaration of the general partner accepting liability for the accuracy of the dossier; Luxembourg substance records (lease agreement, payroll, board minutes).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital transfers arriving from crowdfunding platforms, Apple IAP or Google Play settlement accounts with aggregated payers and no single client invoice.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed Apple Developer Programme and Google Play Distribution Agreements; PSP (Stripe/Adyen/Worldline) monthly payout reconciliation reports; webtoon licensing and multilingual syndication contracts with worldwide distributors; SCSp partnership agreement and LEI certificate; monthly revenue-per-title dashboard exports showing the commercial logic of the aggregated flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible digital business model flagged as 'lack of physical economic footprint' or potential intellectual-property monetisation anomaly.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: ISIC 9000/NACE 90.0 artistic-creation business statement; registered copyright, trademark and domain certificates; user-subscription analytics and adjusted-revenue reports; reviewed or audited financial statements of the SCSp prepared by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises; Luxembourg VAT (TVA) registration number and periodic VAT returns.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid pass-through distributions to foreign artists, letterers and translators, appearing as possible layering or round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Creator/translator agreements with royalty schedules; value-chain and transfer-pricing documentation; recurring board resolutions authorising the distribution policy; monthly payment registers matching outbound MT103s to the underlying generator contracts; CLTIR self-assessment forms where Luxembourg corporate income tax is technically triggered; economic-substance file of the SCSp.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Proposed use of FX derivatives (forwards, swaps or NDFs) causing the bank to assess speculative intent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Treasury policy restricted to hedging forecasted USD/KRW revenue; signed ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and Credit Support Annex; board-minuted hedging mandate with maximum notional limits; quarterly FX exposure mark-to-market reports prepared by the bank's own dealing desk confirming net economic exposure.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Partner capital is wired via SWIFT MT103 (or SEPA Transfer within EUR) to the SCSp's dedicated capital-contribution escrow account at the Luxembourg bank. The remittance must carry the SCSp's LEI, the partnership act date, and the BCL balance-of-payments statistical purpose code falling under 'direct investment' / 'equity capital' in the BCL nomenclature; the unformatted remittance field must explicitly state 'contribution to partnership capital - SCSp - no consideration'. The bank additionally requires the subscribed capital schedule of the partnership agreement and, before funds can be released to the operating account, a compliance clearance confirming the inbound funds are unrelated to third-party receivables; where the capital injection is a treasury transfer from an affiliated company, an intercompany loan or capital-contribution resolution and CRS/FATCA self-certifications of the transferring company must accompany the instruction.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For syndication royalties, creator advances and licensing fees, the primary clearing rail is the SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer (or ISO 20022 pain.001 within SEPA), with BCL balance-of-payments category 'royalties and licence fees' entered in the purpose code field and structured creditor reference (RF/SCOR) identifying the generating contract. For high-value physical comic-book distribution to bookstores and wholesalers, an irrevocable documentary credit under UCP 600 can be established: the Luxembourg bank issues/advises an MT700 LC with presentation of commercial invoices, transport documents, and copies of distribution licences. MT202 COV alongside MT103 messages is used for intercompany funding between the SCSp and its foreign sub-entities, always accompanied by a tax-valid intercompany agreement to satisfy Luxembourg substance and transfer-pricing expectations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards (EUR-USD, EUR-KRW, EUR-JPY) under an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement and the applicable Credit Support Annex or local bank master agreement

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted-settlement currencies such as KRW or INR (offshore NDF tenors up to 12 months) with EU/UK authorised swap counterparties, subject to EMIR reporting/clearing thresholds and board-approved notional limits

Cross-currency swaps (XCCY) and short-dated FX swaps for duration-matched conversion of USD-denominated webtoon subscription cash flows into EUR operating liquidity, governed by ISDA CSA collateral methodologies and the EU Margin Rules (VM/IM) where applicable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of UBO (beneficial owner) information in the Luxembourg Business Registers (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after the anniversary of the RCS registration date; update within 30 days of any ownership change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update incurs administrative fines up to EUR 250; repeated non-compliance may lead to criminal fines up to EUR 1,250 and disqualification of managers, but does not cause strike-off for an SCSp

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Confirmation of registered office and general partner details in the Commercial Register (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change to registered office, general partner, or authorised representative; annual re-confirmation not statutorily required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late amendments subject to court-imposed fines (EUR 25 to EUR 1,000); persistent failure to keep RCS data accurate may attract administrative sanctions from the Attorney General's office

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (applicable only if the SCSp has an economic activity exceeding micro-entity thresholds or if the general partner is a corporate entity requiring consolidated accounts)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the end of the financial year (if mandatory); standard SCSp is exempt because it lacks legal personality
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: If mandatory and not filed, penalties up to EUR 100 per day; for transparent SCSp not subject to the filing obligation, no sanction applicable

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory statutory audit for a standard SCSp in its own name because it is a transparent partnership without legal personality. If the SCSp would qualify as a 'large entity' under Luxembourg law (balance sheet total exceeding EUR 8,800,000; net turnover exceeding EUR 17,500,000; average staff exceeding 250 in two consecutive years) or if a contractual audit covenant is triggered, an independent audit is required.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (plan comptable général luxembourgeois) applied on a pass-through basis; IFRS permitted for consolidated or voluntary filings if the general partner is a Luxembourg entity; annual accounts for partners' reporting under EU Transparency Directives may follow IFRS if mandated.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Luxembourg law does not impose an annual separate UBO return for SCSp. Within 30 days of any transfer or change of limited partnership interests or control rights, an update must be submitted to the RBE. As a best practice, the compliance officer shall prepare an annual internal confirmation letter documenting UBO identification, reviewed before the RCS anniversary, and stored in the statutory books.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Share Transfers and Buyback Transactions
Register of Directors / General Partner Appointments
Register of Decisions and Written Resolutions
Minute Book of General Partners' meetings

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 2,700 - 5,400 (EUR 2,500 - 5,000) per year for a professional registered office and corporate secretarial services in Luxembourg
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,500 - 21,000 (EUR 10,000 - 20,000) for a voluntary or covenant-triggered audit; smaller engagements for SCSp with low activity may start at USD 6,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined corporate income tax headline for Luxembourg collective entities (15% corporate income tax plus solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax); 0% tax at SCSp entity level because the SCSp is fiscally transparent and profits are attributed to partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp level taxation is nil for income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax under the ordinary transparent partnership regime. Qualifying digital IP and webtoon-related software/copyright income may benefit from the Luxembourg IP preferential regime (80% net qualifying income exemption) where nexus and substance conditions are satisfied; such relief is generally claimed by the partner, not by the SCSp itself.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 552 (Luxembourg collective income tax return) filed electronically through MyGuichet.lu / eCDF portal managed by the Luxembourg direct tax administration (Administration des contributions directes). A fully transparent SCSp is not independently taxable, but Form 552 or a parallel partnership allocable-income schedule may be filed on look-through basis where Luxembourg-resident partners are subject to tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Generally 30 June of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; extensions are routinely available for e-filed returns through the tax advisor portal, not later than 31 December of the filing year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1a: Partner identification and profit allocation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter full legal name, Luxembourg registration number, tax identification number, country of tax residence, percentage interest, and profit/loss allocation ratio of each SCSp partner.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must be identified with their foreign tax identification number and treaty residence; exclude their allocable income unless it is attributable to a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg-source webtoon/digital activity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Describe the digital webtoon publishing and multilingual chapter unlocking business, including app store distribution, subscription revenue, and content syndication agreements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State clearly whether the non-resident limited partner operates through a Luxembourg permanent establishment; if no PE exists, note that the activity is outside Luxembourg taxing jurisdiction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2: Webtoon gross revenue and deductions
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report gross receipts from Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, direct webtoon subscriptions, syndication fees, and advertising; deduct platform commissions, content production, translation, distribution, legal fees, and amortization of qualifying digital copyright assets.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If all activities are performed outside Luxembourg for non-resident partners, report no Luxembourg-source income; if a Luxembourg fixed place of business exists, apply arm's-length allocation of revenue and costs between Luxembourg and foreign partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3: Tax adjustments and IP regime calculation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconcile accounting profit to taxable income; apply permanent/temporary differences, and compute any qualifying 80% IP deduction on digital copyright/software-related income supported by nexus documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners should only claim Luxembourg IP deductions on income properly taxable in Luxembourg; otherwise the deduction is reserved for Luxembourg resident partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclose all controlled transactions with related parties, including webtoon licensing royalties, intercompany management fees, and app-store revenue sharing among affiliated companies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach local file/master file schedules where group turnover or controlled transaction thresholds are met; non-resident counterparties must demonstrate beneficial ownership and economic substance or face deduction denial.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or incorrect filing may trigger a late-filing penalty of up to EUR 5,000, an administrative surcharge of up to 10% of the additional tax assessment, monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%, and, for deliberate misdeclaration, tax-fraud penalties and criminal prosecution with fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on dividend payments by Luxembourg collective tax entities; 0% withholding tax on ordinary profit distributions by a transparent SCSp, because such distributions are characterized as partnership profit allocations rather than dividends.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the beneficial owner must submit a completed Form 270 or equivalent reduced-withholding application to the Luxembourg direct tax administration before payment, accompanied by a valid tax residence certificate from the treaty jurisdiction, evidence of beneficial ownership, and substance documentation such as premises, staff, and board minutes. Refund applications are available where tax was withheld at source; processing depends on the relevant DTA and may require EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive proof where applicable.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: 0% Luxembourg withholding tax on outbound royalties and interest under domestic law generally; treaty rates also typically provide 0% withholding for interest and royalties where the recipient is the beneficial owner, provided the arrangement has economic substance and is not recharacterized as a hidden equity contribution.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File/CbCR documentation is triggered where the multinational group's consolidated annual turnover exceeds EUR 750 million; Local File retention is recommended for any related-party transaction exceeding EUR 5 million in annual aggregate controlled turnover, and is mandatory on demand where the SCSp or its partners engage in controlled cross-border digital-content, royalty, financing, or management-fee transactions.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not impose formal GCC-style Economic Substance Regulations, but substance-over-form, ATAD general anti-abuse rules, beneficial ownership principles, and tax ruling requirements apply in full. An SCSp engaged in webtoon syndication must demonstrate genuine commercial purpose, effective management and decision-making in Luxembourg, physical presence, personnel, and real economic activity to preserve treaty network access and avoid recharacterization as an artificial conduit.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Misdeclaration of Digital Revenue
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underreporting or omitting Apple IAP, Google Play Billing, webtoon subscription, or syndication revenue, or deliberately shifting digital profits to non-cooperative zero-tax structures without economic justification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax assessment, monthly late-payment interest at 0.6%, administrative penalties up to 10% of the understated tax, and in criminal cases fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment for up to five years; directors or managers involved in the false declaration may be jointly and severally liable.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing is available where the SCSp is used as a sham; directors, the general partner, and authorized tax representatives may be required to pay unpaid tax personally, face asset seizure, travel restrictions, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp as a conduit without employees, premises, active management, or real business function solely to obtain treaty benefits or to route webtoon IP royalties to another jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and Luxembourg tax residence advantages, application of GAAR/ATAD anti-abuse measures, retroactive reassessment, refusal of deductions, and possible nullity of the arrangement for tax purposes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who establish or maintain a hollow SCSp may be held civilly liable for the unpaid tax consequences, including clawback of royalties and interest, and may face director disqualification and travel bans.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the SCSp to receive, commingle, or launder proceeds from webtoon distribution or to conceal beneficial ownership of the partnership interests or app-store payment accounts; failing to maintain an accurate Luxembourg UBO register.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Anti-money-laundering penalties of up to EUR 5 million for the legal entity and up to EUR 250,000 for individuals, imprisonment up to five years, freezing of app-store payout accounts, and removal of professional authorizations; false UBO declarations carry separate fines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing general partner and compliance officers can be personally fined and imprisoned; directors may be barred from serving in Luxembourg companies and may have personal assets confiscated.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Misalignment / Unapproved Margin Architecture
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to apply arm's-length pricing to intercompany webtoon licensing, digital content royalties, management fees, or financing between the SCSp, its general partner, and non-resident affiliates; documentation that contradicts actual economic substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax adjustments to the Luxembourg taxable base, disallowance of excessive deductions, penalties of 10% to 30% of the adjusted underpayment, late-payment interest, and in intentional cases tax-fraud criminal liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and tax representatives who certify false transfer-pricing documentation face joint and several liability for the resulting tax deficiencies; civil fraud actions may pierce the corporate veil and reach personal assets.
